result.topic_en: Euler tests further forms αxx+βyy (7xx+5yy, 15xx+7yy, 57xx+yy) against his criterion for suitable forms, then begins Example I: deciding whether N = 100003 = 10·100²+3·1² is prime by asking whether it has a second representation as 10xx+3yy.

§. 16. Sit propoſita formula $7xx + 5yy$ et in hac expreſſione $35 + zz$ valores ipſi $z$ tribuendi erunt: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, qui praebent hos numeros: 36, 39, 44, 51, 71, 99, 116, ubi cum adeo ſex ſint compoſiti, hanc formam omnino excludi oportet.

§. 17. Habeatur formula $15xx + 7yy$ et in expreſſione $105 + zz$ ipſi $z$ tribuendi erunt hi valores ad 105 primi: 1, 2, 4, 8, 11, 13, 16, 17, qui praebent hos numeros, omnes pro primis habendos: 106, 109, 121, 169, 226, 274, 361, 394 unde ſequentes formulae in claſſem idoneorum ſunt ponendae: $105xx + yy$; $35xx + 3yy$; $21xx + 5yy$; $15xx + 7yy$.

§. 18. Addamus his exemplis examen formulae $57xx+yy$: et numeri loco $z$ ſucceſſive ſcribendi, ſcilicet 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 hos praebent valores formae $57 + zz$ notatu dignos: 58, 61, 73, 82, 106, 121, 157, 178, 226, qui omnes ſunt vel primi, vel quadrati vel dupli primorum, ita ut formula propoſita certe ſit inter idoneos referenda.

§. 19. Haec ſufficient ad inſignem ſimulque facillimum uſum noſtrae regulae illuſtrandum, cujus ope caſus idoneos formulae $\alpha xx+\beta yy$ ab ineptis diſcernere valemus; qua igitur regula ſtabilita, illos caſus optimo cum ſucceſſu adhibere poterimus ad numeros quosvis in talibus formulis contentos, utrum

ſint primi nec ne, perſcrutandos. Propoſito ſcilicet numero quocunque N facile erit illum pluribus modis ad talem formam $\alpha xx + \beta yy$ reducere, quo facto talis eligatur caſus, qui per regulam ſupra datam non excludatur, ac diſpiciatur, utrum ille numerus N unico tantum modo, an vero pluribus, in hac forma contineatur. Priore enim caſu certe erit primus, poſteriori vero compoſitus, cujus factores ope methodi ſupra traditae facile aſſignare licebit.

Exemplum I.

§. 20. Proponatur numerus $N = 100003$, qui manifeſto in forma $10xx + 3yy$ continetur, exiſtente $x = 100$ et $y = 1$. Videamus ergo, an iſte numerus adhuc alio modo in eadem forma contineatur. Hunc in finem ponamus $100003 - 3yy = 10xx$, atque ut diviſio per 10 ſuccedat, ponatur $y = 1 + 10z$, hincque orietur $10000 - 6z - 30zz = xx$, ſive facta adhuc diviſione per 4 erit $2500 - \frac{3}{2}z - \frac{15}{2}zz = \frac{xx}{4}$.
Hinc igitur, prouti $z$ fuerit vel par vel impar, formemus duos caſus principales. Pro primo ſcilicet ſit $z = 2a$, orietur aequatio $A = 2500 - 3a - 30aa = \frac{xx}{4}$. Pro altero caſu ſit $z = 2b - 1$, orietur iſta: $B = 2494 + 27b - 30bb = \frac{xx}{4}$.

items.quote: hinc concludimus formulam propoſitam, perinde ac ſequentes inde deſumtas, ſcilicet: $40xx + 3yy$; $24xx + 5yy$; $15xx + 8yy$, tanquam idoneas ſpectari debere et in examine tuto admitti poſſe.
items.english: Hence we conclude that the proposed formula, as well as the following ones derived from it, namely 40xx+3yy, 24xx+5yy, 15xx+8yy, must be regarded as suitable and may safely be admitted in the test.

items.quote: ubi cum adeo ſex ſint compoſiti, hanc formam omnino excludi oportet.
items.english: Since as many as six of these are composite, this form (7xx+5yy) must be excluded entirely.

items.quote: unde ſequentes formulae in claſſem idoneorum ſunt ponendae: $105xx + yy$; $35xx + 3yy$; $21xx + 5yy$; $15xx + 7yy$.
items.english: Hence the following formulas are to be placed in the class of suitable ones: 105xx+yy, 35xx+3yy, 21xx+5yy, 15xx+7yy.

items.quote: ita ut formula propoſita certe ſit inter idoneos referenda.
items.english: So the proposed formula 57xx+yy must certainly be counted among the suitable ones.

items.quote: Priore enim caſu certe erit primus, poſteriori vero compoſitus, cujus factores ope methodi ſupra traditae facile aſſignare licebit.
items.english: In the former case (N represented in only one way) it will certainly be prime, in the latter composite, and its factors can easily be found by the method given above.

items.quote: Videamus ergo, an iſte numerus adhuc alio modo in eadem forma contineatur.
items.english: Let us see, then, whether this number (100003) is contained in the same form in yet another way.

items.quote: Hinc igitur, prouti $z$ fuerit vel par vel impar, formemus duos caſus principales.
items.english: Hence, according as z is even or odd, let us form two principal cases.
